messages:
pm-brynn: Quick sync — we got multiple customer asks this week about the chat endpoint shape. Two camps: (1) messages-first (roles+history) and (2) prompt-first (single prompt with metadata). Need to decide prioritization, launch criteria, and migration risk.
eng-jun: Summary: messages-first matches modern chat UX and tool calling flows, but prompt-first is simpler for existing completions users.
ux-alex: Customer feedback: product teams want explicit role semantics (system vs assistant) so moderation + persona enforcement is easier. They also asked for a clear migration path.
sre-mike: Operational ask — messages-first typically increases token-size due to history envelopes which impacts latency/cost. We need a default prefix-caching strategy to hit latency SLOs.
research-eli: From evals: structured tool outputs + function calling are more robust with message arrays because you can attach metadata per message. Also helps with regen and targeted replay.
pm-brynn: Proposed plan: ship messages-first as the primary public shape for chat, but provide a small compatibility shim for prompt-first (server-side conversion). Launch criteria: 1) SDK parity (js/py), 2) clear migration guide + linting tool, 3) perf baseline (p95 latency within 10% of current completions for typical convo sizes), 4) deterministic behavior for system role.
eng-jun: Implementation notes: server-side conversion should accept an optional `prompt` field and expand to messages internally: {"role":"user","content": prompt}. But we must be explicit about how we handle multiple system directives in prompt-first payloads.
ux-alex: UX: provide `system` as special top-level field in prompt shim to reduce ambiguity: e.g. {system: "You are a helpful assistant", prompt: "..."}. That keeps simple clients minimal changes.
sre-mike: We should also add autoshrink batching: if message history exceeds token threshold, auto-trim older assistant/user turns but keep system. Add telemetry to track when this happens.
research-eli: Evals for regression detection: include a sentinel prompt set with 3 categories: persona, hallucination, tool fidelity. Must pass gating thresholds before GA.
pm-brynn: Rollout strategy: 1) opt-in beta for existing API keys flagged `chat-shape-v2`, 2) whitelist a few enterprise customers for feedback, 3) gradual default flip with 2-week warning and compatibility logs.
eng-jun: Backwards compatibility: we can't silently change existing completions endpoints. Shim only when `compat_mode=true` or when `prompt` is present. Otherwise return 400 with migration hint.
ux-alex: Docs + migration tooling: small CLI `rw-migrate-chat` that scans code for completions->chat diffs and suggests changes. Ship with examples for common frameworks.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary start 2026-05-04T02:00Z -> monitor token cost delta, p95 latency, error rate.
pm-brynn: Risks: customers with complex prompt templating might break; we need template-compat tests. Also legal/moderation teams must sign off on system-role enforcement behavior.
research-eli: One more: structured output suggestion — include optional `response_schema` top-level in messages shape so downstream parsers can validate. This intersects with function calling. Need product decision now or later?
eng-jun: Recommendation: include `response_schema` as opt-in GA feature tied to function-calling plumbing. Keep MVP of messages shape without mandatory schema.
pm-brynn: OK — action items: eng to prototype shim + caching (eng-jun), research to run regression evals (eli), UX to draft migration CLI spec (alex), ops to define telemetry & canary thresholds (mike). I'll collect updates in the next sync. :thumbsup:
